issue.description:
NOTE: this is a DELIBERATE BEHAVIOR CHANGE. It contradicts the parent's blanket "no intended behavior change", which only holds for the already-wired in-memory path. Investigation during the split found the streaming PUT path has NO compression wired today, so the streaming round-trip case cannot pass without new wiring.

Finding: putObjectStreaming (internal/server/handlers/handlers.go L462-651) records plaintextSize as the data region (L524 NewEnvelopeHeader), computes envelopeSize from plaintext (L549), encrypts the raw temp file via encryptor.EncryptStream (L567), never calls crypto.CompressStream, never calls header.SetCompressed(), and omits the metadata Compressed field (L593-603). So a >10MB PUT is always stored uncompressed even with ARMOR_COMPRESS=true. crypto.CompressStream already exists (internal/crypto/compress.go L59) with unit coverage (compress_test.go).

Part 1 - Implement opportunistic compression in putObjectStreaming, mirroring the in-memory path (handlers.go L354-377): when h.config.Compress, compress the temp-file plaintext via crypto.CompressStream (streams src->dst, returns the compressed byte count; keep only when strictly smaller than plaintextSize). When kept: header.SetCompressed(); pass the COMPRESSED length (not plaintextSize) as the data-region size into NewEnvelopeHeader; recompute envelopeSize over the compressed size; set metadata Compressed=true; and feed the compressed bytes into encryption (note EncryptStream currently reads tmpFile directly - compress tmpFile into a second temp and EncryptStream over that, recompute blockCount/HMAC-table size over the compressed length). When not smaller, store uncompressed (current behavior). Preserve plaintextSHA over the ORIGINAL plaintext - GET verifies that digest against the decompressed bytes.

Part 2 - Add the streaming round-trip test (extends the harness from the prior children): subtest streaming_compressible - PUT an >10MB compressible payload (above the in-memory threshold at handlers.go L297) with cfg.Compress=true; assert X-Armor-Streaming: true on the PUT, GET body byte-identical to plaintext, stored envelope IsCompressed()==true and header.PlaintextSize < len(plaintext), metadata Compressed==true, GET X-Armor-Compressed: true. Also assert an incompressible >10MB payload round-trips stored UNCOMPRESSED (pass-through).

The GET path already decompresses flagged objects (handlers.go L960-989 + L882-884) - no GET change is needed; the flag set in Part 1 is what activates it.

Acceptance:
- go test ./internal/... passes; streaming_compressible green; the in-memory cases from the prior children still green.
- A streaming PUT with ARMOR_COMPRESS=true stores a flagged, strictly-smaller compressed object that round-trips byte-identical; an incompressible streaming payload passes through uncompressed.
- Label: split-child. Depends on the harness + pass-through children (split-child #1 and #2).
issue.title: Wire streaming PUT zstd compression and add streaming round-trip test

RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet ./... && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...

- docker build succeeds on clean HEAD with no B2/Cloudflare credentials available
- Build time increase is acceptable (<~2 min extra); document the gate in a Dockerfile comment

issue.description:
Scope: the invariants/merge section of docs/research/format-migration-failure-recording-flow.md. Depends on armor-bdf3c257.

Content (two related statements the doc must make precisely):
1. Single-writer invariant: each failure is written to fm.state exactly ONCE, at the failure site (under stateMu). There is exactly one writer of failure data per run. The completion merge (lines ~343-347) deliberately merges ONLY ProcessedObjects and SkippedObjects; FailedObjects and Failures are NOT re-merged because re-merging would double-count every failure (state already has them from the failure sites).
2. Context: this invariant is what TestFormatMigrationFailureRecording asserts (exactly 1 failure recorded — it catches both regressions: 0 from forgetting the failure-site write, and 2 from re-merging at completion). Note the tree's history here: two parallel fix lineages shipped opposite-but-valid forms (failure-site writes vs merge-only writes); the current tree is failure-site writes, so do not 'fix' the doc back to describing merge-only accumulation.

Acceptance:
- Doc states the single-writer invariant explicitly
- Doc explains WHY the completion merge excludes failure data (double-count prevention)
- Doc does not describe the merge as also accumulating failures
- Every line citation in the section grep-verified at edit time
- Commit only docs/research/format-migration-failure-recording-flow.md
issue.title: Document completion-merge exclusion and single-writer invariant in format-migration flow doc

issue.description:
## Task
Read and understand the current error handling path in internal/server/format_migration.go Migrate() function (lines 256-266).

## Investigation
- How failed objects are counted (result.FailedObjects increment at line 258)
- How failures are recorded in the failures list (recordFailure call at line 259)
- Whether state.FailedObjects is being updated correctly (lines 260-262)
- Identify the exact code path where migrateObject() errors should trigger failure recording

## Acceptance
- Document the current error handling flow
- Identify where the gap is (why failures are not being recorded)
- Confirm that recordFailure() function exists and works correctly
issue.notes:
VERDICT DELIVERED BY armor-319ea357 (2026-09-03), from docs/research/format-migration-failure-recording-flow.md ("Verdict" section + addendum).

GAP ANSWER: NO failure-recording gap exists. Pinned to HEAD 9b6d55cd8 (source byte-identical to ca061558f, where the doc re-verified every citation line-by-line; the doc's own pin is ec19626b5). Evidence, internal/server/format_migration.go: recordFailure (:879) has exactly two callers — the metadata-fetch site :239 and the migration-failure site :305; each writes its single record into fm.state under stateMu in the same iteration (:245-248 and :311-314), and an exhaustive grep finds no other mutation of state.FailedObjects/state.Failures. The completion merge (:339-350) merges only Processed/Skipped (:345-346) and deliberately excludes failure data (:347-349), so the returned result — copied from state, not summed (:356-362) — cannot double-count. Persistence covers every exit path: start, every 100 objects (:324-329), interruption (:203), completion (:352). All three regression guards pass at this HEAD (go test ./internal/server/, run 2026-09-03): TestFormatMigrationFailureRecording (format_migration_test.go:988 — asserts exactly 1 failure on both the result and the persisted state), TestFormatMigrationFailurePersistenceRoundTrip (:1061), TestFormatMigrationFailedObjectsNotRetried (:1471).

NO-RETRY IS BY DESIGN: both failure sites call advanceCursor — :249 (with continue at :250) on the metadata-fetch path, :322 in the shared tail on the migration-failure path — so a failed object is never retried, not later in the same run and not on a resumed run: the persisted cursor in .armor/migration-state.json makes the skip stick across restart. The failure itself stays on state.Failures with its reason for operator inspection. This is intended best-effort semantics, pinned by TestFormatMigrationFailedObjectsNotRetried — not an unrecorded failure and not a gap.

PREMISE IS STALE: the premise this bead was written under — "failures not recorded", cited as Migrate() lines 256-266 — is stale as of ec58ea96. At current source those lines hold version-parsing/skip logic, not the failure-handling path; evaluate this bead against the verdict above, not the original line citations.

RESIDUAL GAPS: NONE. Both historical gaps (stale recordFailure comment; interruption losing failures recorded since the last periodic save) are closed in behavior AND in code — the corrected recordFailure comment is committed at :873-878 as of ca061558f. No new bead filed; nothing to link to armor-d3162d1a, because no processed/skipped/failed count-bookkeeping defect exists.
issue.title: Analyze migration failure handling in format_migration.go

issue.description:
RE-SPLIT child 3 of 4 for bf-bmk0ur. SCOPE: the git-reasoning step — produce a rigorous tag->source-commit map for the high-patch tags, the formal version of the lineage reasoning that closed child bf-2efei0 did only loosely.

CONTEXT: HEAD = 43dcd14f68959544461b334a2a280d1b8111e223 (from bf-3jq7hy; NOT clean — internal/server/server.go has +12/-1 uncommitted). VERSION at repo root = 0.1.1905. The armor-build resolve-version quirk means a re-trigger computes patch+1 from the PRIOR VERSION rather than reading VERSION, so tags like 0.1.1906 can be the SAME source as VERSION=0.1.1905.

TASK:
- Walk the VERSION file history (git log -p -- VERSION) and the main branch log to determine, for tags 0.1.1905, 0.1.1906, 0.1.1923: which git commit was main-HEAD when each was built. Use commit timestamps vs the tags' last_updated (from bf-n1g61w: 0.1.1906 pushed 2026-08-09 22:40 UTC; 0.1.1923 older, ~8/7).
- For each tag, record the candidate source commit AND compute git merge-base <commit> 43dcd14f to confirm it is a true ancestor of HEAD (i.e. HEAD is at-or-ahead of that source).
- Explicitly determine: was ANY existing tag built from a commit at-or-after HEAD 43dcd14f? (Expected answer: NO — 43dcd14f was committed 00:14 UTC 8/10, after the last build at 22:40 UTC 8/9.)

ACCEPTANCE: a comment with a table: tag -> source commit -> merge-base vs HEAD 43dcd14f -> (ancestor? yes/no). Plus a one-line verdict on whether any tag is at-or-ahead of HEAD.
issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-tt5o44]
TAG -> SOURCE-COMMIT MAP (timestamp + merge-base proof; HEAD=43dcd14f, VERSION@root=0.1.1905)

METHOD: resolve-version auto-bumps push to the GitHub MIRROR only, so auto-bumped tags
(0.1.1906 ... 0.1.1923) are INVISIBLE in Forgejo VERSION history. Commit 95cc29b9 documents
this: "a commit that sets VERSION takes the other branch and pushes nothing." Only the manual
bump to 0.1.1905 lands at 892bd314 (0.1.1903 -> 0.1.1905, skipping 0.1.1904). So tags are mapped
to source commits by correlating each push time to main-HEAD-at-that-instant; ancestry is then
PROVEN by merge-base.

| tag      | source commit | src commit time (UTC) | VERSION carried | merge-base vs 43dcd14f | ancestor of HEAD? |
|----------|---------------|-----------------------|-----------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| 0.1.1905 | 892bd314      | 2026-08-07 14:09:42   | 0.1.1905        | 892bd314 (=src)        | YES               |
| 0.1.1906 | d390fdf1      | 2026-08-09 18:42:24   | 0.1.1905        | d390fdf1 (=src)        | YES               |
| 0.1.1923 | f9b22955 *    | 2026-08-08 00:37:37   | 0.1.1905        | f9b22955 (=src)        | YES               |

* 0.1.1923 push time is only known as "~8/7", so its source is the [892bd314..f9b22955] range
  (the 8/7 burst of re-triggers walking patch+1 off the prior published tag: 0.1.1906 -> ... ->
  0.1.1923). f9b22955 is the last commit in that window (8/7 20:37 EDT = 8/8 00:37 UTC), so the
  highest patch of the burst most likely maps to it; cannot be pinned to a single SHA without an
  exact push timestamp. Either way it is a strict ancestor of HEAD.

PER-TAG RATIONALE:
- 0.1.1905: MANUAL VERSION bump at 892bd314. A commit that sets VERSION builds that value
  as-is -> source = 892bd314.
- 0.1.1906: pushed 2026-08-09 22:40 UTC. At that instant main-HEAD was d390fdf1 (committed
  18:42 UTC); the NEXT commit 5e93d15c did not land until 23:50 UTC, and b0530757/43dcd14f
  after that. So 0.1.1906 source = d390fdf1, which STILL carries VERSION=0.1.1905 (unchanged
  since 892bd314). This is the resolve-version quirk: the re-trigger computed patch+1 off the
  VERSION FILE (0.1.1905) -> 0.1.1906, NOT off the registry-high path. This is exactly why
  0.1.1906 < 0.1.1923 despite being LATER (patch numbers non-monotonic in build order). The
  task note "0.1.1906 can be the SAME source as VERSION=0.1.1905" holds for the VERSION *value*;
  the actual git commit is d390fdf1 (a descendant of 892bd314), not 892bd314 itself.
- 0.1.1923: see * (8/7 patch-walk burst).

ANCESTRY PROOF: for each source commit C, `git merge-base C 43dcd14f` returns C own SHA -> C
lies on HEAD first-parent history -> C is a true ancestor, HEAD strictly ahead. (Divergence
would return an earlier common ancestor, not C.)

VERDICT: NO existing tag is at-or-ahead of HEAD 43dcd14f. Every source commit is a proper
ancestor (merge-base == self, ancestor_of_HEAD=YES). HEAD was committed 2026-08-10 00:14:47 UTC,
AFTER the latest build (0.1.1906 @ 22:40 UTC 8/9). HEAD leads the newest tag source d390fdf1 by
3 commits (d390fdf1 <- 5e93d15c <- b0530757 <- 43dcd14f), none of which any published image was
built from. Building HEAD now would ship genuinely new code absent from every existing tag.

[migrated comment from bf-tt5o44, 2026-08-10T06:59:06.626384548Z, author cli]
TAG -> SOURCE-COMMIT MAP (child 3 of bf-bmk0ur): rigorous lineage version.

METHOD: source commit = the main-branch tip at each tag's registry push time (last_updated from bf-n1g61w), i.e. newest commit with committer-date <= push time. Ancestry confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <src> 43dcd14f`.

HEAD = 43dcd14f, committed 2026-08-10 00:14:47 UTC (= 20:14:47-04 on 8/9).

| tag      | pushed (UTC)          | source commit | source ctime (UTC)             | merge-base vs HEAD 43dcd14f | ancestor of HEAD? |
|----------|-----------------------|---------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| 0.1.1923 | 2026-08-07 12:21:09   | cdea76eb      | 2026-08-07 09:34:49 (05:34-04) | cdea76eb                     | YES               |
| 0.1.1905 | 2026-08-07 14:57:43   | 892bd314      | 2026-08-07 14:09:42 (10:09-04) | 892bd314                     | YES               |
| 0.1.1906 | 2026-08-09 22:40:25   | d390fdf1      | 2026-08-09 18:42:24 (14:42-04) | d390fdf1                     | YES               |

VERDICT (one line): NO existing tag is at-or-ahead of HEAD -- every published image is strictly BEHIND 43dcd14f; the newest tag by push (0.1.1906 @ 22:40 UTC 8/9) is from d390fdf1, and HEAD landed 00:14:47 UTC 8/10 (~1h34m after the last push), so commits 5e93d15c / b0530757 / 43dcd14f (and the parallel 81fb084a) are in NO image.

SUPPORTING DETAIL:
- resolve-version quirk confirmed exactly: 0.1.1906 = patch+1 of VERSION 0.1.1905. VERSION has been 0.1.1905 since 892bd314 (8/7); the d390fdf1 build left VERSION untouched so resolve-version auto-bumped to 1906. => 0.1.1906 is the SAME source lineage as VERSION=0.1.1905, just the +1 applied.
- 0.1.1905 source = 892bd314 (the commit that explicitly sets VERSION 0.1.1903->0.1.1905); pushed 48 min later. Excluded 8551f5ec: committed 14:57:53 UTC, 10 sec AFTER the 0.1.1905 push (14:57:43), so correctly out of that build.
- 0.1.1923 is the HIGHEST patch number but the OLDEST of the three (pushed 8/7 12:21) -> patch number is non-monotonic vs push time, confirming the quirk. Source = cdea76eb (SecondaryBackend field, ADR-006), the tip in the 09:34-13:42 UTC gap on 8/7.
- DAG caveat (bf-4lw9u4 parallel-ship): 81fb084a has the same subject as d390fdf1 and was committed 41s earlier (18:41:43 UTC) but is NOT an ancestor of d390fdf1 -- it rode a parallel branch merged later by b0530757 (23:52 UTC), AFTER the 0.1.1906 push, so it was NOT in the 0.1.1906 tree. d390fdf1 is the true first-parent former main tip.

No file changes (verification-only). Git tags in this repo are only v0.1.0/v0.1.7/v0.1.8 -- these are Docker Hub image tags (ronaldraygun/armor), mapped via VERSION/git lineage as the memory note prescribes (no OCI labels, no iad-ci build runs).

issue.close_reason:
Implemented Version 2 counter space overflow protection:

1. Added validation to Encryptor (checkCounterSpace and checkCounterSpaceWithStart methods):
   - Computes blockCount * (blockSize / 16) as uint64 before uint32 storage
   - Returns explicit error when >= 2^32 with message: "object exceeds the Version 2 counter space; envelope v3 removes this limit"
   - Called in Encrypt(), EncryptStream(), EncryptWithStartingCounter()

2. Added validation to CompleteMultipartUpload handler:
   - Checks total block count won't overflow before completing multipart uploads
   - Surfaces as S3 InternalError (500) with specified message

3. Added comprehensive unit tests (counter_space_test.go):
   - Tests at boundary (2^20 blocks = 64 GiB at 64 KiB blocks)
   - Tests different block sizes (4 KiB, 64 KiB, 256 KiB)
   - Tests multipart starting counter validation
   - Tests exact boundary condition (counter = 2^32 - 1)

All tests pass. The validation prevents keystream reuse from counter wrap at 64 GiB for Version 2 encryption.
issue.description:
Plan §8.1. Version 2 stores blockIndex*(blockSize/16) in a uint32 (encryptor.go makeCounter): at 64 KiB blocks it wraps at 2^20 blocks = 64 GiB, after which keystream repeats.

Do: in the encryptor (and the multipart CompleteMultipartUpload validation), compute blockCount*(blockSize/16) as uint64 and return an explicit error ("object exceeds the Version 2 counter space; envelope v3 removes this limit") when >= 2^32. Surface as S3 InternalError with that message.

Acceptance: unit test with a synthetic block index at the boundary; PutObject/UploadPart tests for the error; go test ./... passes.
issue.title: Refuse Version 2 writes whose block count would wrap the 32-bit CTR field

Thread-safety verification complete. expvar.Map.Add IS thread-safe for concurrent increments from multiple goroutines.

Key findings:
1. Package documentation explicitly states: 'Operations to set or modify these public variables are atomic.'

2. Map.Add implementation uses sync.Map for concurrent-safe access:
   - sync.Map.LoadOrStore() is atomic
   - addKey() is protected by keysMu sync.RWMutex

3. The underlying Int type uses atomic.Int64.Add() for thread-safe increments:
   type Int struct {
     i atomic.Int64
   }
   
   func (v *Int) Add(delta int64) {
     v.i.Add(delta)
   }

Source: https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/refs/heads/master/src/expvar/expvar.go

The implementation provides full thread-safety guarantees for concurrent Add() calls from multiple goroutines.

Test patterns analyzed and documented. Key findings:

1. Two test approaches exist: Harness tests (direct HTTP + SigV4) and Lifecycle tests (AWS SDK v2)

2. PUT Pattern: Create test data → PUT request → Sign → Execute → Verify HTTP 200 + store ETag

3. GET Pattern (already implemented): GET request → Sign → Execute → Verify using helpers (assertGETSuccess, assertGETContentEqual, assertGETMetadata)

4. DELETE Pattern: DELETE → Verify HTTP 204 → Triple-check 404 (GET+HEAD+LIST)

5. GET Helper Functions added in b71b4ebf: parseGETResponse, assertGETSuccess, assertGET404, assertGETContentEqual, assertGETMetadata

6. Test lifecycle: PUT → GET verify → DELETE → 404 verify

7. Use byte patterns for verification: bytes.Repeat, modulo sequences (i % 256), 0xAA/0xBB patterns

8. Test multiple scenarios: sizes, compressed/uncompressed, ranges, multipart

- Backend interface: ListMultipartUploads(ctx, bucket, prefix) - NO key-marker/upload-id-marker params

- Handler only echoes key-marker in response (line 2909) but doesn't use it for backend call

Sibling ListObjectVersions pattern (CORRECT):
- Backend interface: ListObjectVersions(..., keyMarker, versionIDMarker, ...) - HAS marker params  
- Handler (lines 2957, 2971): reads key-marker, applies prefix: backendKeyMarker := h.applyPrefix(keyMarker)
- Handler (line 2973): passes backendKeyMarker to backend

This is a real bug preventing pagination from working when ARMOR_PREFIX is configured. The fix requires:
1. Add keyMarker/uploadIDMarker params to backend.ListMultipartUploads interface
2. Update B2, filesystem, nil backend implementations
3. Update handler to read and pass markers to backend

The restoreViaARMOR function now provides a truly separate decrypt implementation from restoreViaDirectDecrypt: it reads the full raw ciphertext object in one GetRange call (vs. multiple calls in the direct path), extracts encrypted data and HMAC table differently for single-PUT vs multipart layouts, and uses internal/crypto directly for decryption. Both paths must agree for known-good data, which the regression test TestVerifyObject_DualPathAgreeOnKnownGoodData confirms. This resolves the guaranteed false-positive SHA-256 mismatch on every ModeDual run for real ARMOR-encrypted objects. Committed as ab75bfc0.

Investigation determined that current ARMOR architecture cannot support arbitrary non-uniform multipart parts (Barman's chunk_size + N*512 pattern). The block-based decryption architecture requires that no block spans multiple parts, but non-block-aligned parts would create exactly this condition. Each part's contribution to a boundary block is encrypted with different CTR offsets, making the concatenated block impossible to decrypt as a single unit.

The existing part-1/final-part exemptions (fc6c1a86) already resolve the immediate outage for databases that fit in one part. For larger databases requiring multiple parts, the solution is to restrict non-uniform parts to block-aligned sizes only (multiples of 64KB), which allows parts to vary in size while preserving the block-based decryption architecture.

Barman options:
1. Patch barman-cloud-backup to pad parts to 64KB boundaries
2. Use single-part exemption with large --min-chunk-size (current production configuration)

detail.reason: Fixed TestCompleteMultipartUploadRecoversAmbiguousBackendSuccess by correcting the size comparison in the ambiguous multipart completion recovery path. The handler was incorrectly comparing the on-disk ciphertext size (which includes HMAC overhead) against the sum of plaintext part sizes, causing a 500 InternalError. Added totalCiphertextSize calculation that accounts for HMAC overhead (32 bytes per 64KB block) and updated the recovery validation at handlers.go:3132 to use the correct ciphertext size for comparison. The test now passes and the handler correctly recovers from NoSuchUpload by validating the assembled object size before finalizing metadata via CopyObject.

detail.reason: Fixed: CompleteMultipartUpload recovery ciphertext size calculation was incorrect. For multipart uploads, B2 assembles only encrypted part data (same size as plaintext). The HMAC table is stored separately as a sidecar file (.armor/hmac/<sha256(key)>) and is NOT included in the assembled object. The handler was incorrectly adding HMAC overhead (32 bytes per block) to totalCiphertextSize, causing the ambiguous-backend-success recovery path to reject a valid assembled object when info.Size != totalCiphertextSize. Fix: Remove HMAC overhead from totalCiphertextSize calculation.

Implemented MEK ring infrastructure and documentation for rs-manager ARMOR rotation

## What was implemented:

1. **Documentation** (docs/notes/mek-rotation-2026.md):
   - Complete 4-phase rotation procedure
   - OpenBao commands for key ring setup (operator-executed)
   - Kubernetes manifest update instructions

   - Verification and monitoring procedures

   - Added ARMOR_MEK_RING env var to armor-deployment.yml (optional, respects existing ring if present)
   - Added MEK_RING ExternalSecret mapping in armor-externalsecret.yml

## What remains (operator action):

The actual key rotation requires OpenBao write access to:
1. Retrieve current MEK and generate new MEK
2. Update OpenBao with new ring structure (current MEK → ring, new MEK → active)
3. Update escrow with both keys
4. Wait for ArgoCD sync (automatic)
5. Trigger rotation via POST /admin/key/rotate through kubectl proxy
6. Poll GET /admin/key/ring until objects_by_fp shows 0 under old fingerprint
7. Verify canary health and test object decryption

## Infrastructure ready:

The deployment is now ready to consume the MEK_RING from OpenBao. Once the operator updates the secret values in OpenBao, ExternalSecret will sync them to Kubernetes, ArgoCD will apply the deployment update, and the rotation can proceed through the admin API.

## References:

- Plan §8.13: MEK key ring design
- Plan §8.1: Cipher correctness (why rotation is critical for V1 disclosure)
- ADR-005: CTR keystream reuse vulnerability

No keys entered agent context during this work — all procedures use stdin redirects and file descriptors.

detail.title: Range GET on a non-uniform (ADR-011) multipart v2 object never routes to offset-aware decryption

detail.reason:
Fixed in commit 739b49bc (pushed to origin/main). Two bugs in the ADR-011
non-uniform multipart read path:

1. internal/crypto/decryptor.go DecryptRange verified every block's HMAC
   unconditionally. A non-uniform part's boundary block (trailing partial
   block, or a part starting mid-block) carries a placeholder all-zero HMAC
   from UploadPart time (no single part call ever saw the whole block's
   ciphertext to hash for real) -- the full-object read path already knew
   to skip these (isPlaceholderHMAC in handlers.go), but DecryptRange (every
   range-GET) didn't, so it 500'd on exactly the block whose HMAC was never
   computed. Added the same isPlaceholderHMAC skip to the crypto package.
   Decryption itself needed no change -- CTR is correct regardless of which
   part a byte arrived in.

2. decryptNonUniformParts fed decrypted plaintext straight into wholeHash,
   but CompleteMultipartUpload stores CombinePartPlaintextSHAs' combined
   per-part digest, not a plain whole-object SHA-256 and not the fixed-P
   MultipartDigestAccumulator chunking (which doesn't line up with a
   non-uniform object's real part boundaries). Fixed by hashing each part
   and feeding that digest into wholeHash instead, and excluding
   isNonUniform from useCombinedDigest.

Fixed double-counting bug in format migration skip logic

The issue was on lines 275-287 of internal/server/format_migration.go, where two separate skip conditions could both be true for the same object, causing SkippedObjects to be incremented twice.

Example scenario from TestFormatMigrationV2Skipped:
- V2 object with includeVersions=["1"] and currentWriteVersion=2
- First check: version 2 is NOT in ["1"] → SkippedObjects++ (first increment)
- Second check: version 2 IS at target (2==2) → SkippedObjects++ (second increment)
- Result: 2 skips instead of 1

The fix combines the two conditions into a single OR check:
if uint8(version) == fm.currentWriteVersion || !fm.shouldMigrateVersion(uint8(version))

This ensures mutually exclusive skip counting - an object is skipped once for one combined reason, not twice for separate reasons.
